annotations.description: Playing Secluded Steppe (which enters tapped) on turn 1 instead of Plains or Swamp is suboptimal. With Orzhov Basilica in hand (which also enters tapped and bounces a land), the ideal sequencing is to play an untapped land on turn 1, then play Orzhov Basilica on turn 2 (bouncing the untapped land back to replay later). Playing the tapped land first means turn 2 Basilica would bounce the Steppe back (wasting the tapped entry), or if they play another land turn 2 instead, they're behind on mana. Additionally, Secluded Steppe could be better saved for cycling later in the game when land drops are less critical. Playing Plains turn 1 would allow smoother sequencing with Orzhov Basilica on turn 2 (bouncing Plains, replaying it turn 3 untapped) and keeps the cycling option available for later.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Secluded Steppe (enters tapped) as turn 1 land drop.
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains (enters untapped) on turn 1, then Orzhov Basilica on turn 2 bouncing Plains, preserving Secluded Steppe for later cycling or as a future land drop.

annotations.description: Playing Plains instead of Orzhov Basilica on turn 2 is suboptimal. Orzhov Basilica enters tapped and bounces a land, but playing it now (bouncing Secluded Steppe) would give access to WB mana on turn 3 with just the Basilica, effectively ramping. With Plains, the player has two lands that each produce one mana. With Basilica, they'd have one land producing two mana (WB) and Secluded Steppe back in hand to replay next turn, ending up with 3 mana on turn 3 instead of 2. This enables casting Orzhov Advokist on turn 3 (needs 2W) by playing the returned Steppe or another land. With Plains played now, they'll have only 2 mana on turn 3 unless they play another land. Actually, they'd play a land on turn 3 either way - but with Basilica they'd have Basilica (WB) + replayed land = 3 mana on turn 3, and with Plains they'd have Steppe + Plains + turn 3 land = 3 mana on turn 3 as well. However, Basilica produces 2 mana from one land, so on turn 4 they'd have more total mana available. Playing Basilica on turn 2 bouncing Secluded Steppe, then replaying Steppe turn 3, gives 3 mana turn 3 and 4 mana turn 4. Playing Plains turn 2, then Basilica turn 3 bouncing Steppe, gives 2 mana turn 3 (Basilica tapped) and then 4 mana turn 4. So playing Basilica first avoids the tempo loss of having it enter tapped on a later turn when you want to cast spells like Citadel Siege or Orzhov Advokist.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Plains as land drop on turn 2
annotations.betterLine: Play Orzhov Basilica, bouncing Secluded Steppe back to hand, then replay Secluded Steppe on turn 3 to have 3 mana available on turn 3 instead of losing tempo later when Basilica enters tapped

While next turn's plays still work with either land, subsequent turns casting larger spells like Verdant Sun's Avatar become harder with a colorless land taking up a land drop.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Rogue's Passage as the land for the turn
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp to improve colored mana base, saving Rogue's Passage for a later turn when colored mana requirements are better covered

annotations.description: With only 3 mana available (Plains, Orzhov Basilica, Swamp), casting Orzhov Advokist uses all mana for the turn. Casting Arcane Signet for 2 mana instead would leave 1 mana unused this turn but accelerate future turns significantly, enabling 4-mana plays next turn (like Citadel Siege or Bold Plagiarist with a land drop, or Cunning Rhetoric). Orzhov Advokist's upkeep trigger won't fire until Gem3Flash's next upkeep anyway, so the tempo gain from the Signet is more impactful. Additionally, playing the Signet first allows casting the Advokist next turn alongside another spell or holding up mana for Bold Plagiarist (flash). The Advokist is a fine card but doesn't need to come down immediately when ramp is available.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Orzhov Advokist for 3 mana, using all available mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Arcane Signet for 2 mana, saving 1 mana and enabling stronger plays next turn (e.g., Cunning Rhetoric + land, or Citadel Siege with 4+ mana, or holding up Bold Plagiarist at flash speed).

annotations.description: Acidic Slime costs {3}{G}{G} (5 mana) and could be cast this turn to destroy a problematic permanent like Crown of Doom (which punishes you when attacked) or an opponent's key land. Soul of Innistrad is a 6/6 deathtouch for 6 mana, but there are no creatures in Gemini2.5Flash's graveyard to recur, making its activated ability irrelevant for now. Additionally, casting Acidic Slime would also trigger Karametra to fetch a land, ramping toward casting the more expensive cards next turn. The Odric/deathtouch synergy works with either creature (Acidic Slime also has deathtouch), and destroying Crown of Doom specifically would remove a persistent threat that buffs attackers targeting you.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Soul of Innistrad for 6 mana (using Caves of Koilos for 1 life), getting a 6/6 deathtouch with no graveyard targets to recur.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Acidic Slime for 5 mana to destroy Crown of Doom (or another problematic permanent), trigger Karametra for a land, and save mana/life. Soul of Innistrad could be cast next turn with better mana available and potentially graveyard targets later.

annotations.description: Fetched a Forest when a Plains would have been better. The player already has 2 Forests (sufficient green for Acidic Slime at 3GG), but only has Caves of Koilos as a white source. Fetching Plains would enable casting Sunblast Angel (4WW) sooner by providing a second white source, while still having enough green for Acidic Slime.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched Forest from library with Karametra trigger
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Plains to get a second white source, enabling both Acidic Slime (already castable) and Sunblast Angel (needs WW) in upcoming turns.

annotations.description: Attacked Gem3Flash where Orzhov Advokist (1/4) can block Odric (3/3) and survive, resulting in 0 damage dealt. Meanwhile, attacking Devstral would grant +2/+0 from Crown of Doom, making Odric a 5/3, likely dealing 5 damage unblocked (Devstral probably wouldn't want to chump with Reef Worm since it triggers death cascades).

annotations.betterLine: Attack Devstral to benefit from Crown of Doom's +2/+0 bonus, dealing 5 damage with a likely unblocked Odric.

annotations.description: Devstral activated Crown of Doom to give it to another player. Crown of Doom gives +2/+0 to creatures attacking you, which is a downside for the controller. However, activating it costs {2}, and Devstral only has 4 Islands available (Crown of Doom is already on the battlefield). By spending 2 mana on this activation, Devstral is left with only 2 mana remaining. The problem is that Crown of Doom is actually a symmetrical/political card - giving it away means the new controller's opponents get +2/+0 when attacking that player. But the real issue is that Devstral is spending 2 mana to give away an artifact that was actually protecting them somewhat (discouraging attacks) and could have instead held up mana or cast Stroke of Genius for X=1 to draw a card at end of turn. More importantly, the Crown of Doom's downside (+2/+0 to attackers against you) is not that significant at this point in the game, and spending 2 mana proactively during main phase to pass it is questionable when Devstral could use that mana more productively. With Reef Worm as a blocker and no immediate threat of being attacked, this activation seems like wasted mana that could have been used for Stroke of Genius X=1 at end of turn for card advantage.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Crown of Doom for {2} to give control of it to another player.
annotations.betterLine: Pass without activating Crown of Doom, hold up 4 mana to cast Stroke of Genius for X=1 at end of opponent's turn to draw a card, maintaining card advantage while keeping mana flexible.

annotations.description: Devstral is giving Crown of Doom to GPT-4.1-mini, who has Sangromancer (a 3/3 flyer) that could attack Devstral. Crown of Doom gives +2/+0 to creatures attacking its controller, so giving it to GPT-4.1-mini means creatures attacking GPT-4.1-mini get +2/+0. However, Gemini2.5Flash has more board presence with Odric and Karametra and is arguably a bigger threat. Giving Crown of Doom to Gemini2.5Flash would incentivize other players to attack Gemini2.5Flash (since their attackers would get +2/+0), which helps keep the strongest board in check. GPT-4.1-mini has fewer creatures and less board development, so incentivizing attacks against them is less strategically valuable. That said, GPT-4.1-mini does have a flyer that could attack Devstral, and the Crown makes attacking GPT-4.1-mini more attractive for others, which could redirect aggression. This is debatable but sending Crown to Gemini2.5Flash seems slightly better given their stronger board state.
annotations.actionTaken: Gave Crown of Doom to GPT-4.1-mini
annotations.betterLine: Give Crown of Doom to Gemini2.5Flash to incentivize attacks against the player with the strongest board (Karametra, Odric)

annotations.description: Devstral is sending Crown of Doom to Gemini2.5Flash, who has Orzhov Advokist on board. Orzhov Advokist encourages opponents not to attack Gem3Flash (by offering +1/+1 counters in exchange for a non-aggression pact). Crown of Doom punishes whoever controls it by giving +2/+0 to creatures attacking them. Sending it to Gemini2.5Flash seems reasonable since they're a threat with Karametra and Odric, but GPT-4.1-mini has Sangromancer (flying 3/3) which could be more immediately threatening. The choice between the two targets is debatable - Gemini2.5Flash has more board presence with Karametra (indestructible enchantment that will ramp when creatures are cast) and Odric, making them arguably the better target. However, Gemini2.5Flash's lands are all tapped, meaning they may struggle to pass Crown of Doom to someone else soon, which is good. This seems like a reasonable choice, but sending it to GPT-4.1-mini who has Sangromancer (a creature that could attack Devstral and benefit from the +2/+0) might have been slightly better to discourage attacks from that direction. Overall this is close to reasonable.
annotations.actionTaken: Sent Crown of Doom to Gemini2.5Flash
annotations.betterLine: Could have sent Crown of Doom to GPT-4.1-mini instead, who has an untapped Sangromancer that could attack and benefit from the +2/+0 boost. However, the choice is debatable.

annotations.betterLine: Choose Dragons mode to tap down opponent threats each combat, providing immediate defensive value while rebuilding board presence

annotations.description: Gemini2.5Flash casts Abzan Ascendancy while Verdant Sun's Avatar is on the stack. The Avatar hasn't resolved yet, so Abzan Ascendancy's +1/+1 counter ETB trigger won't apply to the Avatar (it's already on the battlefield by the time Ascendancy resolves, but the ordering is: Ascendancy resolves first giving +1/+1 to existing creatures, then Avatar resolves and enters). Actually, since Avatar is on the stack, Ascendancy would resolve first, putting +1/+1 counters on existing creatures (Odric and potentially Karametra if it's a creature). Then Avatar resolves and enters. The key question is whether casting Abzan Ascendancy now vs. after Avatar resolves matters. If cast now, Ascendancy's ETB puts counters on Odric (and Karametra if devotion is high enough). Then Avatar enters and triggers life gain equal to its toughness. If cast after Avatar resolves, Ascendancy would also put a counter on the Avatar. So casting it now means the Avatar doesn't get the +1/+1 counter from Ascendancy's ETB. This is a minor sequencing issue - waiting to cast Ascendancy after Avatar resolves would have given the Avatar a +1/+1 counter too. However, the bigger concern is that all lands appear tapped - it's unclear how Abzan Ascendancy is being cast with tapped lands. Looking more carefully, Verdant Sun's Avatar is on the stack (being cast), and the player's lands are shown as tapped, suggesting the Avatar cast used most mana. The Abzan Ascendancy costs WBG and Sol Ring could help, but everything appears tapped. This may be a game engine allowing the cast with floating mana. The sequencing of casting Ascendancy while Avatar is on the stack (before it resolves) means Avatar won't get the +1/+1 counter from Ascendancy's ETB.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Abzan Ascendancy while Verdant Sun's Avatar was still on the stack
annotations.betterLine: Let Verdant Sun's Avatar resolve first, then cast Abzan Ascendancy so the Avatar also receives a +1/+1 counter from Ascendancy's ETB trigger

annotations.description: Gemini2.5Flash has Verdant Sun's Avatar on the stack (about to resolve), and Sunblast Angel in hand. Verdant Sun's Avatar is a creature spell being cast, which means Karametra's trigger will search for a Forest or Plains. But the critical issue is that they are attacking with ALL creatures before Verdant Sun's Avatar has resolved. Looking more carefully - the Verdant Sun's Avatar is on the stack, meaning it was already cast. The game is asking to select attackers during precombat main with a spell on the stack, which is unusual. But the key strategic issue is: they have Sunblast Angel in hand (6 mana, destroys all tapped creatures on ETB). By attacking with everything, they're tapping all their own creatures. If they later cast Sunblast Angel, it would destroy their own tapped attackers. More importantly, they're sending Acidic Slime (2/2 deathtouch) and Odric (who gives keyword sharing) into combat when opponents have blockers. Devstral has a 6/6 Whale token that could block and kill non-deathtouch creatures. GPT-4.1-mini has Sangromancer (3/3) and gains life from creature deaths. The 'all attack' is reckless - they should be more selective about which creatures to attack with and which opponents to target. Attacking Karametra (7/8 indestructible) is fine, Soul of Innistrad (7/7 deathtouch) is strong, but sending the 2/2 Acidic Slime into combat is risky for little gain, and Odric sharing deathtouch to all attackers is valuable but also puts the 4/4 at risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all creatures (Odric 4/4, Karametra 7/8, Soul of Innistrad 7/7, Acidic Slime 3/3)
annotations.betterLine: Be more selective with attacks. At minimum, hold back Acidic Slime (a 2/2 that already provided its ETB value and is a weak attacker). Consider holding back creatures to preserve board state, especially with Sunblast Angel in hand as a future play that punishes tapped creatures - you don't want your own creatures tapped when you might want to cast it.

annotations.description: Gemini2.5Flash is attacking Gem3Flash (31 life) with Odric, Lunarch Marshal (3/3). Meanwhile, Devstral has a 6/6 Whale token and only 4 tapped Islands with no untapped blockers. Attacking Devstral would deal 3 damage to a player who could become threatening with the Whale token (which will produce a 9/9 Kraken if it dies). Additionally, Gem3Flash at 31 life is far from being eliminated by a single 3-damage attack, so the reasoning of 'trying to take them out' doesn't hold up well. However, Gem3Flash is the lowest life total player and politically it's not unreasonable to pressure them, so this is debatable.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked Gem3Flash with Odric (3 damage to a 31-life player)
annotations.betterLine: Consider attacking Devstral instead, as they have a dangerous Whale token on board and pressuring them keeps their life total in check. Alternatively, the attack into Gem3Flash is fine politically but the reasoning of 'taking them out' at 31 life with 3 damage is flawed.

annotations.description: Devstral has exactly 4 Islands (all tapped from a previous phase, but this is their main phase on their turn). The Shaper Parasite costs {1}{U}{U} to cast face-up, requiring 3 mana. Casting it as Morph costs {3}, also requiring 3 mana. However, casting face-up reveals information and commits the -2/+2 or +2/-2 trigger immediately. With Verdant Sun's Avatar on the stack (belonging to Gemini2.5Flash), there's no immediate threat that needs the Shaper Parasite's face-up trigger right now. Casting as Morph would preserve the option to use the trigger at a more opportune time (e.g., when an opponent attacks or when a better target presents itself), and the surprise factor of a face-down creature has value. The face-up cast gives the same 2/3 body but forces the trigger now when there may not be a high-value target. Additionally, casting face-down keeps the opponent guessing about what it is.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Shaper Parasite face-up
annotations.betterLine: Cast Shaper Parasite face-down as a Morph for {3}, preserving the flexibility to use the +2/-2 or -2/+2 trigger at a more impactful moment

annotations.description: GPT-4.1-mini is resolving Pulse of Murasa (return target creature or land card from a graveyard to hand, gain 6 life) while Verdant Sun's Avatar is on the stack. Even Orzhov Advokist or Reef Worm from opponents' graveyards would be better picks. Returning a land they can't even use effectively is a clear waste of the card selection.

annotations.description: GPT-4.1-mini is casting Verdant Sun's Avatar (on the stack, about to resolve) and attacking with Sangromancer in the same turn. Attacking before the Avatar resolves means Sangromancer won't benefit from any combat-relevant considerations, but more importantly, the Avatar is a 5/5 that could attack this turn if it had haste (it doesn't). However, the real issue is attacking with Sangromancer (a 3/3 flyer) into a board where Devstral has a 6/6 Whale token and Gemini2.5Flash has Odric (3/3) plus Karametra (6/7 indestructible, though likely not a creature yet). The Crown of Doom gives +2/+0 to creatures attacking GPT-4.1-mini, which is GPT-4.1-mini's own artifact - it doesn't affect GPT-4.1-mini's attacks. Sangromancer has flying so it can likely get through against most opponents. But the key concern is that GPT-4.1-mini chose 'All attack' when only Sangromancer is available (Verdant Sun's Avatar is still on the stack, not on the battlefield yet). Actually, looking more carefully, the Avatar is on the stack during the precombat main phase - this means GPT-4.1-mini cast the Avatar and is now being asked about attackers. The Avatar hasn't resolved yet if it's still on the stack during attack selection... Actually no, the message says 'Select attackers' with Verdant Sun's Avatar on the stack - this is unusual. It's likely the Avatar was cast and will resolve, and now we're in combat. Attacking with just Sangromancer (flying 3/3) is fine - it can fly over blockers. This seems reasonable overall.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all available creatures (Sangromancer 3/3 flying)

Verdant Sun's Avatar is on the stack (being cast by GPT-4.1-mini), and Bold Plagiarist's ability only triggers when opponents put counters on creatures they control - it doesn't interact with the Avatar. Meanwhile, Citadel Siege (Khans mode) from Gemini2.5Flash's board or future counter-placement could be relevant, but the immediate timing concern is that casting a 2/2 creature with flash during your own precombat main is suboptimal - flash creatures are better held for opponents' turns for surprise blocks or to react to counter-placement. Bold Plagiarist specifically wants to be held up as a surprise response when an opponent puts counters on their creatures.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Bold Plagiarist during own precombat main phase with all mana tapped
annotations.betterLine: Hold Bold Plagiarist and pass turn, keeping it available to flash in during an opponent's turn when they put counters on creatures (e.g., Orzhov Advokist triggers, Citadel Siege triggers, or Breena triggers). The flash is the key advantage of this card and casting it on your own turn wastes that surprise value.

The real issue is that spending 2 mana to pass Crown of Doom to another player is questionable value - it just moves the downside to someone else temporarily while costing Devstral mana they could use for other things. With a hand full of expensive spells (Fool's Demise at 5, Hoverguard Sweepers at 8, Sphinx at 7), every mana matters. Additionally, the Crown of Doom only punishes the controller when creatures attack them, and Devstral has a 6/6 Whale token that's a decent blocker. The mana would be better saved for future turns to cast their powerful spells sooner.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Crown of Doom's ability for {2} to give it to another player.
annotations.betterLine: Pass without activating Crown of Doom, saving mana (or the option of playing the Island from hand) to work toward casting powerful cards like Fool's Demise or Shaper Parasite sooner. The Crown of Doom's downside is manageable with the 6/6 Whale token as a blocker.

annotations.description: Devstral is attacking with only the 2/3 Shaper Parasite instead of the 6/6 Whale Token (or both). The Whale Token represents significant damage pressure. GPT-4.1-mini has Sangromancer (3/3 flying) which can't block the ground Whale, and Gem3Flash has no creatures. Gemini2.5Flash has Odric (3/3) and Karametra (not a creature unless devotion ≥ 7). There's also a Verdant Sun's Avatar on the stack belonging to some player. Attacking with just a 2/3 is very low impact compared to swinging with the 6/6, and there's no obvious reason to hold back the Whale Token defensively given the board state. The Whale dying creates a 9/9 Kraken, so even trading in combat would be favorable.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only the 2/3 Shaper Parasite, holding back the 6/6 Whale Token.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with the 6/6 Whale Token (and possibly the Shaper Parasite too) to pressure opponents. The Whale has a death trigger that creates a 9/9 Kraken, making it safe to attack aggressively.

annotations.description: GPT-4.1-mini cast Ancient Craving (pay 3 life, draw 3 cards) while Verdant Sun's Avatar is on the stack. The Avatar (5/5) will trigger and gain 5 life when it enters, and Sangromancer is on board. At 45 life, the 3 life loss is negligible. However, the player has Essence Pulse in hand which gives -X/-X where X = life gained this turn. If the Avatar resolves first (gaining 5 life), and then Essence Pulse is cast (gaining 2 more life for total 7 life gained), it would be a -7/-7 board wipe. By casting Ancient Craving now (before Avatar resolves), the player is using 4 mana that could potentially be saved, though they only have 2 untapped lands (Forest and Swamp) plus the tapped ones. Looking more carefully at the mana situation: they have Forest (untapped), Swamp (untapped), and Rogue's Passage - that's only 2 colored mana available, not enough for Ancient Craving ({3}{B}) or Essence Pulse ({3}{B}). Wait - looking at the board again, there's a Swamp tapped, Forest untapped, Crown of Doom, Swamp untapped, Talisman of Resilience tapped, Rogue's Passage, Sangromancer, Forest tapped. So 1 Forest + 1 Swamp + Rogue's Passage untapped = 3 mana. They can't cast Ancient Craving with just 3 mana... Unless this is happening with the stack resolution giving priority and they already had mana floating. Actually, the system offered Ancient Craving as a valid choice, so presumably they can cast it. The land drop (Swamp in hand) hasn't been played yet. They should play the Swamp first to have more mana available - but actually the choice 'Unknown' might be the land play. Playing a land before casting the spell would give them more options. This sequencing issue (casting a spell before playing a land from hand) is a minor concern.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Ancient Craving for {3}{B} while Verdant Sun's Avatar was on the stack, potentially before playing the Swamp from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play the Swamp from hand first to maximize available mana, then decide whether to cast Ancient Craving or hold mana open for Essence Pulse (which could be a powerful board wipe combined with Verdant Sun's Avatar's life gain trigger).

annotations.description: GPT-4.1-mini activated Rogue's Passage (costing 4 mana and tapping it) while Verdant Sun's Avatar is on the stack and hasn't resolved yet. The activation requires a target creature, but the timing is during the resolution of casting VSA. More importantly, spending 5 mana total (4 + tap) to make a creature unblockable during their own precombat main phase before even declaring attackers is premature, and the mana spent on Rogue's Passage could have been better used. Additionally, Sangromancer is a 3/3 flyer - making it unblockable is of marginal value since it already has evasion via flying. The Crown of Doom activation (passing it to an opponent) or simply passing priority would have been better.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Rogue's Passage to make a creature unblockable, spending 4 mana and tapping the land, while Verdant Sun's Avatar was still on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority without activating either ability, preserving mana and Rogue's Passage for a more impactful moment. Sangromancer already has flying for evasion.

annotations.description: Sunblast Angel's ETB (destroy all tapped creatures) appears to have no valid targets - no creatures on the board are tapped. The player's reasoning states it will 'clear the board of tapped threats' but there are none. While a 4/5 flyer is decent and triggers Karametra, casting it precombat purely for a board wipe effect that won't happen is suboptimal. Additionally, deploying creatures before combat when you could attack first (potentially tapping blockers with combat) is generally worse sequencing.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Sunblast Angel expecting to destroy tapped creatures when none are tapped
annotations.betterLine: Attack first with Odric (potentially getting creatures tapped as blockers), then cast Sunblast Angel post-combat to destroy any newly tapped blockers. Alternatively, consider holding Sunblast Angel for a turn when opponents' creatures are more likely to be tapped.

annotations.description: Chose a basic Plains over Canopy Vista when Canopy Vista would enter untapped (they control multiple basic lands) and provides both green and white mana, giving strictly more flexibility.
annotations.actionTaken: Fetched a basic Plains
annotations.betterLine: Fetch Canopy Vista, which enters untapped and produces both green and white mana, providing more flexibility for casting both Sunblast Angel (WW) and other spells.

annotations.description: Gemini2.5Flash has Sunblast Angel in hand and Verdant Sun's Avatar on the stack (being cast this turn). Sunblast Angel destroys all tapped creatures when it enters. By attacking with all creatures now, they are tapping their own creatures. If they planned to cast Sunblast Angel later (which they have in hand), their own creatures would be tapped and vulnerable to their own Sunblast Angel's ETB. More critically, the player is attacking with ALL creatures including Odric (who shares keywords like deathtouch from Soul of Innistrad/Acidic Slime/Void Beckoner to all attackers) into a board where Devstral has a 6/6 Whale token that could block, and GPT-4.1-mini has Sangromancer (which gains 3 life per creature death). Attacking everything blindly into multiple opponents without considering who to attack or which creatures to hold back is reckless. Additionally, there's no indication of who is being attacked - sending all creatures at once in multiplayer without strategic targeting wastes the political advantage of selective attacks, and risks losing valuable creatures to blocks while feeding Sangromancer life gain triggers.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all six creatures indiscriminately.
annotations.betterLine: Attack selectively - send large creatures like Karametra (7/8, if active as creature) and Soul of Innistrad at the most threatening opponent, keep some creatures back as blockers, and preserve the option to cast Sunblast Angel post-combat to destroy opponents' tapped creatures while keeping your own untapped. At minimum, hold back some creatures to avoid feeding Sangromancer triggers and to maintain board presence.

annotations.description: Devstral chose Fool's Demise (an aura for creature death insurance) over Intellectual Offering, which would draw 3 cards and untap all nonland permanents. In a multiplayer game at turn 6, card advantage from Intellectual Offering is significantly more impactful than protecting a single creature, especially since the Whale Token already generates a 9/9 Kraken on death.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Fool's Demise (enchant a creature with death recursion)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Intellectual Offering to draw 3 cards and untap permanents, gaining significant card advantage and potentially enabling further plays this turn

annotations.description: Witch's Clinic only produces colorless mana and its lifelink ability is only relevant for the commander (which isn't on the battlefield). With Essence Pulse (3B) and Pulse of Murasa (2G) in hand, colored mana sources are more valuable. The player is already at 45 life with Verdant Sun's Avatar about to gain them more, so the lifelink utility is negligible.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Witch's Clinic, which only produces colorless mana
annotations.betterLine: Play a Forest or Swamp to have more colored mana available for casting Essence Pulse or Pulse of Murasa in upcoming turns

annotations.description: GPT-4.1-mini is casting Essence Pulse while their own Verdant Sun's Avatar is on the stack (about to resolve). Verdant Sun's Avatar is a 5/5 that would gain them life equal to creatures' toughness when it enters. If they let the Avatar resolve first, they'd gain 5 life (from Avatar's own toughness) plus 3 life (from Sangromancer's toughness), making X=8 for Essence Pulse, which would wipe nearly everything. But more critically, Essence Pulse gives each creature -X/-X where X is life gained this turn. If cast now before Avatar resolves, X is only 2 (no life gained yet this turn), meaning Essence Pulse gives all creatures -2/-2. This kills their own Sangromancer (3/3 becomes 1/1... actually survives at 1/1). Wait - at -2/-2, Sangromancer becomes 1/1 and survives, Odric becomes 1/1, the Whale token (6/6) becomes 4/4, Karametra (6/7 but not a creature unless devotion ≥7). Actually the bigger issue is that Essence Pulse is being cast with Avatar still on the stack - Essence Pulse will resolve BEFORE Avatar. With X=2 (only the 2 life from Essence Pulse itself), this barely affects the board. If they waited for Avatar to resolve, Avatar entering would trigger life gain (5 from itself + 3 from Sangromancer = 8 life gained this turn combined with Essence Pulse's 2 = X would be 10), giving -10/-10 to all creatures - a devastating board wipe that kills everything except their Avatar. Instead, casting now with X=2 wastes the Essence Pulse for almost no effect.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Essence Pulse while Verdant Sun's Avatar was still on the stack, resulting in X=2 (-2/-2 to all creatures), barely affecting the board.
annotations.betterLine: Let Verdant Sun's Avatar resolve first. Avatar enters, triggering life gain from itself (5 toughness) and Sangromancer (3 toughness) = 8 life gained. Then cast Essence Pulse gaining 2 more life for X=10 total, giving all creatures -10/-10, wiping the entire board except your own 5/5 Avatar (which becomes -5/-5... actually this kills Avatar too). Still, even with just Avatar's triggers giving 8 life, a -10/-10 wipe removes all opponent threats. Alternatively, just don't cast Essence Pulse at all and keep it for a better opportunity.

annotations.description: GPT-4.1-mini is activating Rogue's Passage for 4+tap to make a creature unblockable, but this is during their precombat main phase while Verdant Sun's Avatar is on the stack (being cast). They're spending 5 mana (4 generic + tapping Rogue's Passage) on making a creature unblockable before the Avatar even resolves. Looking at the board, they have Sangromancer (3/3 flying) which already has evasion via flying, and the Avatar hasn't resolved yet. More importantly, they're tapping lands that could be used for other purposes. The Rogue's Passage activation costs 4 mana plus tapping itself - this is a significant mana investment to make an already-flying Sangromancer unblockable, or to target the Avatar before it resolves. Given that Sangromancer already has flying (natural evasion), spending 5 total resources to make it unblockable is wasteful. They could save those resources for future turns or other plays.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Rogue's Passage ({4}, {T}: Target creature can't be blocked this turn) during precombat main while Verdant Sun's Avatar was on the stack.
annotations.betterLine: Simply tap Rogue's Passage for colorless mana ({T}: Add {C}) if mana was needed, or don't activate it at all. The 4 mana spent on unblockable is wasted when Sangromancer already has flying for evasion, and the Avatar hasn't even resolved yet.

annotations.description: Gemini2.5Flash has Verdant Sun's Avatar on the stack (resolving), which means it's about to enter the battlefield. The player is casting Daring Fiendbonder (a 5/1) while Verdant Sun's Avatar is still on the stack. More importantly, the player has Sunblast Angel in hand (4WW, destroys all tapped creatures when it enters). Looking at the board, Devstral has 4 tapped Islands and a Whale Token (untapped), GPT-4.1-mini has some tapped lands and Sangromancer. Sunblast Angel costs 4WW which the player can't cast with current mana (only 1 Swamp, 3 Forests, 1 Caves of Koilos, 1 Sol Ring = no way to get WW). So Sunblast Angel isn't castable yet. The Daring Fiendbonder is a reasonable play as a 5/1 body, though the player's reasoning about it having 'an extra combat phase' is completely wrong - Daring Fiendbonder gives indestructible from the graveyard, not extra combat. However, playing a creature before combat when Odric is on board is fine since Odric checks at beginning of combat. The bigger concern is whether casting the creature now is good sequencing - with Karametra on the battlefield, casting a creature spell lets you search for a Forest or Plains. This is actually good value. The play itself is reasonable, but casting a 5/1 creature that dies to almost any blocker when you could potentially hold it seems slightly questionable. Also, the player could have equipped Swiftfoot Boots to Odric first for hexproof/haste sharing via Odric's ability.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Daring Fiendbonder (5/1 for 3B) during precombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Could consider equipping Swiftfoot Boots to Odric first (cost {1}) to give all creatures hexproof and haste via Odric's ability at beginning of combat, then cast Daring Fiendbonder. Though mana is largely tapped, so this sequencing point may be moot. The play is defensible but the reasoning was completely wrong about the card's abilities.

annotations.description: Gemini2.5Flash has Sunblast Angel in hand and Verdant Sun's Avatar on the stack (being cast this turn). Sunblast Angel destroys all tapped creatures when it enters. By attacking with all creatures now, they will be tapped after combat. If they then cast Sunblast Angel post-combat, their own tapped attackers would be destroyed. More importantly, they're attacking with ALL creatures including Sunblast Angel itself (which appears to already be on the battlefield based on the choices), meaning they're tapping it unnecessarily. But the bigger issue is that attacking all-out leaves them completely open to counterattacks from multiple opponents. With 6 creatures attacking one player (GPT-4.1-mini at 45 life), they can't kill them this turn (4+7+7+3+8+4 = 33 damage, not lethal against 45 life), while leaving themselves completely defenseless against Devstral's 6/6 Whale token and any plays from Gem3Flash. They should have been more selective about which creatures to send in, keeping some back as blockers.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all 6 creatures (Odric, Karametra, Soul of Innistrad, Acidic Slime, Void Beckoner, Sunblast Angel) for 33 total damage against a 45-life opponent.
annotations.betterLine: Attack selectively - send the biggest threats (Karametra 7/8, Soul of Innistrad 7/7, Void Beckoner 8/8) while keeping Odric, Acidic Slime, and Sunblast Angel back as blockers. This still deals 22 damage while maintaining board presence and defensive capability. Also, holding back Sunblast Angel preserves the option to use it as a board wipe threat later.

annotations.description: Verdant Sun's Avatar is a significant threat that provides ongoing life gain. Devstral chose to deploy a face-down morph creature (Riptide Survivor) instead of using Pongify to destroy the Avatar, turning a 5/5 life-gain engine into a mere 3/3 vanilla token.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Riptide Survivor (likely as a morph) instead of interacting with the Verdant Sun's Avatar on the stack/battlefield.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Pongify targeting Verdant Sun's Avatar to remove the life-gain engine, replacing it with a much less threatening 3/3 Ape token.

annotations.description: Riptide Survivor's value comes from its 'When turned face up, draw three cards, then discard a card' trigger. Casting it face-up means this trigger will never fire, making it just a vanilla 2/1. Casting it face-down via Morph preserves the ability to flip it later for a powerful draw-3 effect, and even gives a bigger 2/2 body initially.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Riptide Survivor face-up as a vanilla 2/1, permanently losing access to its draw-3 trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Riptide Survivor using Morph for {3} as a face-down 2/2, preserving the option to pay {1}{U}{U} later to flip it and draw 3 cards, discard 1.

annotations.description: Equipping Swiftfoot Boots to Karametra gives hexproof and haste, but Karametra is an indestructible enchantment (not currently a creature since devotion to green and white is likely below 7), so the equipment would fall off or provide minimal value. Meanwhile, Verdant Sun's Avatar is on the stack and about to resolve as a 5/5 creature - equipping boots to the Avatar after it resolves would protect a much more vulnerable and valuable creature. Additionally, Odric is also on the battlefield as a creature target that could benefit from hexproof protection. The reasoning mentions giving Karametra haste, but Karametra likely isn't a creature and already has indestructible even if she were.
annotations.actionTaken: Equipped Swiftfoot Boots targeting Karametra, God of Harvests
annotations.betterLine: Wait for Verdant Sun's Avatar to resolve, then equip Swiftfoot Boots to the Avatar (protecting a vulnerable 5/5) or to Odric (protecting the keyword-sharing engine). If Karametra isn't a creature, the equip would be wasted mana.

annotations.description: Equipped Swiftfoot Boots to Karametra, God of Harvests, which already has indestructible, making the hexproof redundant against most removal. Other creatures like Odric (key for keyword sharing) or Soul of Innistrad (6/6 deathtouch, no innate protection) would benefit more from hexproof protection. With Odric on the field, hexproof would be shared to all creatures at combat regardless of which creature has the boots.
annotations.actionTaken: Equipped Swiftfoot Boots to Karametra, God of Harvests (already indestructible)
annotations.betterLine: Equip Swiftfoot Boots to Odric, Lunarch Marshal (protecting the keyword-sharing engine and giving him hexproof+haste) or Soul of Innistrad (protecting a high-value non-indestructible threat)

annotations.description: Gemini2.5Flash is attacking with ALL creatures while Verdant Sun's Avatar is on the stack (meaning it's entering the battlefield this turn and hasn't resolved yet, so it's not among attackers). However, attacking with ALL creatures means attacking with Sunblast Angel, which has 'When this creature enters, destroy all tapped creatures.' Sunblast Angel was apparently just cast this turn (it's on the battlefield but the Verdant Sun's Avatar trigger is on the stack from it entering). More critically, the player is sending every creature into combat with no strategic targeting - they're sending everything at presumably one opponent. With Odric on board giving keyword sharing, all creatures gain deathtouch (from Acidic Slime/Soul of Innistrad/Void Beckoner) and flying (from Sunblast Angel), which is powerful. But the real issue is that Devstral has a 6/6 Whale token that could block, and more importantly, sending ALL creatures leaves zero blockers. GPT-4.1-mini has Sangromancer (gains 3 life when opponent's creatures die) and Crown of Doom (attacking creatures get +2/+0), and the player is at 37 life so not in immediate danger but is leaving themselves completely open. The 'reasoning' of 'All attack! Devstral won't know what hit them!' suggests no actual strategic thought. A more measured approach would be to hold back at least some blockers, especially since multiple opponents could swing back on empty boards.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with all 7 creatures, leaving no blockers
annotations.betterLine: Hold back at least 1-2 creatures as blockers (e.g., Solemn Recruit or Acidic Slime) while still pressing a strong attack. With Odric sharing deathtouch and flying to all attackers, even 4-5 attackers would be devastating. Keeping some defense is important in a 4-player game where you're leaving yourself open to 3 opponents' attacks.

annotations.description: Chose to block with the more valuable Ape Token 3/3 instead of the less valuable Riptide Survivor 2/1. Neither creature can kill the 5/5 attacker, so both die regardless. Preserving the 3/3 body would have been better for future turns.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked with Ape Token 3/3, losing a more valuable creature
annotations.betterLine: Block with Riptide Survivor 2/1 to preserve the larger Ape Token 3/3 for future combat

annotations.description: Devstral blocked with Riptide Survivor (2/1) instead of the Ape Token (3/3). The Ape Token is a vanilla token that blocks better in combat (deals 3 damage instead of 2, survives more attacks with 3 toughness), and is more expendable since it's just a token rather than a real card.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked with Riptide Survivor 2/1
annotations.betterLine: Block with Ape Token 3/3, which deals more combat damage, has higher toughness, and is a more expendable token creature.

annotations.description: Devstral blocked with Riptide Survivor (2/1) instead of the Ape Token (3/3). Riptide Survivor has future value if turned face up (draw 3, discard 2), while the Ape Token is a vanilla creature with no additional upside. Additionally, the 3/3 Ape Token would absorb more combat damage than the 2/1 Riptide Survivor.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked with Riptide Survivor 2/1, sacrificing a creature with potential card advantage upside and absorbing less damage.
annotations.betterLine: Block with the Ape Token 3/3, which absorbs more damage and preserves the more valuable Riptide Survivor for potential future morph activation.

annotations.description: Blocking with the Ape Token 3/3 instead of the Riptide Survivor 2/1. If the attacker would kill either blocker, the 3/3 body is more valuable to preserve than the 2/1. Both would likely die to the same attacker, so losing the bigger token is wasteful.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked with the Ape Token 3/3
annotations.betterLine: Block with the Riptide Survivor 2/1, preserving the more valuable 3/3 body

annotations.description: Played Forest instead of Radiant Fountain. Radiant Fountain would have provided 2 free life which synergizes with Verdant Sun's Avatar's ETB trigger (gaining 5 life) and especially with Essence Pulse in hand, where the total life gained this turn determines the -X/-X effect. Radiant Fountain's 2 extra life would make Essence Pulse -9/-9 instead of -7/-7 if cast this turn, and provides free life value regardless.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest as their land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Radiant Fountain to gain 2 life, synergizing with Verdant Sun's Avatar ETB and Essence Pulse in hand for a larger board wipe effect

annotations.description: Playing Orzhov Basilica on turn 6 bounces a land back to hand, resulting in the same land count on board instead of gaining one. The reasoning states 'It's an excellent turn one play' which is inappropriate for turn 6. With Sunblast Angel (6 mana) and Void Beckoner (8 mana) in hand, maximizing land count is important. Orzhov Basilica enters tapped AND bounces a land, costing tempo compared to playing Plains or Grim Backwoods which would simply add a land.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Orzhov Basilica, bouncing a land back to hand and entering tapped
annotations.betterLine: Play Grim Backwoods (untapped utility land) or Plains to have 7 lands on board instead of 6, getting closer to casting Sunblast Angel or Void Beckoner on subsequent turns

annotations.description: Radiant Fountain would have provided 2 additional life, which synergizes with Essence Pulse in hand. With Verdant Sun's Avatar entering (gaining 5 life), Radiant Fountain would bring total life gained to 7 before Essence Pulse, making Essence Pulse give -9/-9 instead of -7/-7 if cast later. This could be relevant for dealing with larger threats like the 6/6 Whale token.
annotations.actionTaken: Played a basic Swamp instead of Radiant Fountain
annotations.betterLine: Play Radiant Fountain to gain 2 life, synergizing with Essence Pulse's X value for a potential bigger board wipe effect

annotations.description: Gem3Flash chose Swamp when Plains would better support their hand. They have Citadel Siege (2WW) and Oblation (2W) in hand, and already have adequate black mana (Swamp + Orzhov Basilica + Arcane Signet). Adding another Plains would make casting Citadel Siege more reliable and leave more flexible mana for double-spelling turns.
annotations.actionTaken: Chose Swamp as the land to play/put onto battlefield
annotations.betterLine: Choose Plains to better support the white-heavy spells in hand (Citadel Siege at 2WW, Oblation at 2W) since black mana was already sufficient

annotations.description: Playing Swamp instead of Radiant Fountain misses free 2 life that synergizes with Verdant Sun's Avatar (on the stack) and Essence Pulse in hand. Radiant Fountain's life gain would increase the power of a future Essence Pulse and synergize with the life-gain theme. The extra black mana is less relevant with existing black sources available.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Swamp as land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Radiant Fountain to gain 2 life, stacking with Verdant Sun's Avatar's 5 life gain to boost future Essence Pulse to -9/-9 instead of -7/-7

annotations.description: Leyline Prowler would have been a better cast here. It provides mana acceleration (taps for any color), has deathtouch and lifelink (relevant keywords), and would trigger Verdant Sun's Avatar for 3 life on entry. The extra mana production helps cast the Pulse of Murasa and Essence Pulse in hand more efficiently in future turns. Veinwitch Coven's recursion ability requires dealing combat damage, which is harder to leverage immediately.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Veinwitch Coven (3/3 with menace and conditional recursion)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Leyline Prowler (2/3 with deathtouch, lifelink, and mana production) to accelerate future plays and provide better keyword utility

annotations.description: Playing Orzhov Basilica bounces an existing land and enters tapped, resulting in net tempo loss. With Karametra already on the battlefield (triggering off the Verdant Sun's Avatar on the stack to fetch a land), Myriad Landscape would have been strictly better - it doesn't bounce a land, provides mana development, and has a future activation to fetch two basics.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Orzhov Basilica, which enters tapped and bounces an existing land
annotations.betterLine: Play Myriad Landscape instead - no bounce cost, enters as a land, and can later sacrifice to fetch two basic lands for additional ramp

annotations.description: Casting Leyline Prowler while Verdant Sun's Avatar is still on the stack means the Prowler enters before the Avatar resolves. This means Avatar's ETB trigger won't see Prowler's entry, missing out on gaining 3 life (Prowler's toughness). At 45 life this isn't game-changing but it's free value lost.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Leyline Prowler while Verdant Sun's Avatar was still on the stack
annotations.betterLine: Let Verdant Sun's Avatar resolve first, then cast Leyline Prowler to trigger Avatar's ability and gain an additional 3 life. Also should play a land (Sapseep Forest) before or after.
